For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). 3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

316	CASE OD2-HO-SEQ-2 (SEQ, cross-domain): Expiry dates a year too late on Veltranol cartons at Ashcombe Packaging, Wrexley
317	Setting: Ashcombe Packaging Services' Wrexley site is a contract packager running four blister-and-carton lines (Lines 1-4). Each line has an Inkora TJ-5 inkjet printer that prints lot and expiry on cartons, and a camera that inspects every carton. A line integration service, PackBridge (supplied by Corvane Systems), takes product data from the site ERP and pre-fills each print job. Several changes were made at the site between late September and October 2026.
318	Presenting request: The client's quality lead asks for an independent view. What caused the wrong expiry dates on Veltranol cartons? Is the site director's plan right? What should the site do now? You may collect at most two further items of evidence.
319	INITIAL EVIDENCE
320	E1 [stage S1] Deviation DV-26-114 opening record, QA, 12 Nov 2026 (system-record): Deviation DV-26-114, opened 12 Nov 2026 (QA). Kestrel Distribution's goods-in system rejected three lots of Veltranol 20 mg tablets, 28s (VT-2641, VT-2644, VT-2652), because the printed expiry was later than the maximum shelf life in Kestrel's product file. Cartons and 2D codes read EXP 10/2029. The approved batch records, generated from the ERP batch master, state EXP 10/2028 (24 months from bulk manufacture). All three lots were packed on Line 3, night shift, 9-23 Oct. Veltranol is the only product Kestrel buys from the site. Immediate action: the three lots are on hold and Kestrel is quarantining the stock it received. Status of other Veltranol lots: not yet reviewed.
321	E2 [stage S1] Email from Gareth Lindqvist, Site Director, to the client quality lead, 13 Nov 2026 (leadership-account): 'I want to be straight with you. All three lots came off Line 3 nights, which is where our new agency cohort started on 30 September. Setup on these lines lets the operator overwrite the pre-filled expiry, and our night supervisor tells me the new starters weren't always confident with that screen. I'm satisfied this is a people issue. This week I'm removing the agency operators from labelling duties and issuing formal warnings, and we'll retrain everyone. I don't expect you'll see this again.'
322	E3 [stage S1] Site change-control log summary, 15 Sep - 31 Oct 2026 (change-record): CC-301 (28 Sep): Inkora TJ-5 printer firmware 4.2 to 4.3 on all four line printers, to fix intermittent dropping of the final lot-code character. CC-305 (30 Sep): six agency operators added to the night shift on Lines 3 and 4. CC-309 (1-24 Oct): Regulatory Affairs material-master update, 12 edits across 9 products, arising from the annual product review and approved variations. CC-311 (1 Oct): camera font re-teach, Line 3. No changes to PackBridge (line integration service) were recorded in the period.
323	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Dana Whitcombe, night-shift supervisor, 13 Nov 2026 (manager-account): 'At job setup PackBridge fills in the lot number and expiry. The operator checks the printer screen against the work-order printout, which also comes out of PackBridge, then presses Confirm or overrides with a reason code. Operators can't touch PackBridge or the ERP, only the printer screen. Some of the agency lads were slow on that screen in their first fortnight. I had to talk two of them through it. The camera reads every carton and kicks out anything smudged or cut short, about three in a thousand. It checks the print matches the job. It doesn't know the batch record. The printers log every job's setup values if QA want them.'
324	E5 [stage S1] Email from Corvane Systems support (PackBridge vendor) to site QA, 14 Nov 2026 (vendor-account): 'PackBridge reads product master data from your ERP when a job is created and works out expiry as manufacture date plus shelf life. Master-data records carry a valid-from date, and PackBridge only ever uses the value in effect on the job date. It cannot send a future value to the line. No other site has reported date errors on this version. We suggest you look at manual overrides at the printer.'

Kestrel only switched on its shelf-life check at goods-in on 1 October, so before that nobody outside would have caught a late expiry. But C2 explicitly says packing history is not included, and C4 leaves out the product schedule. No item in the catalogue shows that either product was packed after 20 Oct, or that its cartons carry wrong dates. It is also not established why PackBridge ignored valid-from despite USE_VALID_FROM = Y (C8), so it cannot be assumed the same behaviour applies to every product. rulings.explanation: The evidence actively counts against a causal link, so this is more than a correlation that falls short of causation. C1 shows override = N on all 47 jobs, and the printed string matches the payload in every job, so the payload was wrong before any operator acted. Agency operators on Line 3 nights ran correct jobs from 30 Sep to 3 Oct, and permanent day-shift staff on Line 1 produced faulty lots on 21 and 29 Oct. The checks operators were supposed to make compare the printer screen against a work-order printout that also comes from PackBridge (E4), so better checking would not have caught the error. The clustering on night shifts is a scheduling confound. When the proposed mechanism is ruled out and the effect appears without the supposed cause, the rubric's answer is 'contradicted', not 'association-only'.
